discrepancies.description: The canonical policy source (rules.md) is inert; a parallel hardcoded policy source (Council.Constitution + PolicyRegistry) is authoritative at runtime.
discrepancies.evidence: rules.md 225 lines; 19 *.ex hits, all moduledoc prose; zero functional readers. R0_SOURCE_PLAN.txt:221 requires one authoritative versioned policy source.

discrepancies.description: Two of the six PolicyRegistry policies (high_risk, invariant_protection) declare applies_to: [:any] but the matcher tests membership literally, so they can never fire. Risk-based and invariant-based human approval is silently disabled.

The RuleEngine cannot return :approved for any real caller decision type: the built-in scorer emits only :neutral/:violated, capping compliance at 0.70 against a 0.80 approval threshold. The :strengthened verdict exists only in the plugin path, which is never started (PrincipleRegistry is not a supervisor child). Starting it would make :approved reachable for any decision type whose payload carries evidence_count >= 3 and confidence >= 0.7 (EvidenceBeforeConfidence strengthens at weight 1.0), so this defect and the hard-invariant bypass (D-04) must be fixed in that order.
A policy action of :approve pre-commits the decision and score_auth never overrides it, so a RuleEngine hard-invariant violation can be returned as :approved.
discrepancies.evidence: council/policy_registry.ex:113-121 (emergency_halt, action :approve); council.ex:119-126; council.ex:134-143 (score_auth merges score but not decision); rule_engine.ex:242-249 (hard invariants).

discrepancies.description: Authorization.permitted?/1 returns true for :conditional, and MachineAuthorization.mint/2 gates only on permitted?/1, so a conditional decision with unmet conditions can be minted into a machine grant on any path that does not apply the WME conditions check.
discrepancies.evidence: council/authorization.ex:112-114; council/machine_authorization.ex:105; world_mutation_engine.ex:100-133 and :323-329 (the only conditions check).

discrepancies.description: Human approval is a record-only dead end: HumanApprovalQueue.approve/3 writes history and removes the request, and no code path resumes a :requires_human decision. Every human-gated decision is permanently suspended, including CEL.Kernel.restart_service/2 and halt/2.
discrepancies.evidence: council/human_approval_queue.ex:51-64; EXECUTION_CONTRACTS.md:388 (the sibling symptom on the Omega path).

discrepancies.description: The kill-switch module set is never started; world_supervisor calls a non-existent API; SafetyCortex sends to an unregistered name outside a try/rescue; CIS arbitration defaults to :approve.
discrepancies.evidence: grep over the three kill-switch module names returns only definitions and dead world_supervisor calls; multi_world/world_supervisor.ex:111,136,140; cortex/safety_cortex.ex:393 (unguarded) vs :396-400 (guarded); cis/supervisor.ex:240-248.

discrepancies.description: No certificate carries a cryptographic signature, expiry or subject-version binding. The one field named signature is an unkeyed SHA-256 over public fields, and its manifest_id is a hardcoded literal that does not describe the replayed manifest.
The tiannara_audit verifiers are structurally incapable of failing, and the tool has no test directory, so its committed 220/220 PASS report establishes nothing.
discrepancies.evidence: tiannara_audit/lib/tiannara_audit/graph_verifier.ex:23,29,35; proof_verifier.ex:21-22; tiannara_audit/ contains no test/ directory.

discrepancies.description: The federation quorum implementation contradicts its own documented guarantee: trunc(N*0.667) instead of ceil(2/3 N), and votes carry no instance identity or dedup.

Two policy evaluators with different condition grammars (Council.PolicyRegistry and CEL.RuntimePolicyEngine) operate in the same application with no reconciliation, and the institutional CBAC gate plus the authority verifier have zero callers.
discrepancies.evidence: council/policy_registry.ex:15-21 vs cel/policy/runtime_policy.ex + cel/services/runtime_policy_engine.ex; os/governance/capability_checker.ex (0 callers); omega/authority_verifier.ex (0 callers).

discrepancies.description: Three unrelated gate families compete for the name gate (GovernedEffectSink N1-N9, runtime ProductionGateFramework 13 gates, GCK ChronogramGate) and none maps to the seven CAP gates.
discrepancies.evidence: governed_effect_sink.ex:34-70; tiannara_runtime .../certification/gates_06_07_08_09_10_11_12_13.ex:289-505; gck/chronogram_gate.ex:60,63; no 2%/5%/1%/3% thresholds exist.

discrepancies.description: No rollback restores a previously validated state; the rollback_available field still defaults to true at institution_adaptation_result.ex:214, contradicting the contract requirement that non-revocable effects say so at their call sites.
The CEL kernel state machine authorises itself: transition/1 consults only the local transition table, with no Council decision, certificate or policy.
An approved constitutional amendment changes nothing but a version string, and the amended constitution is written to the engine's private copy rather than to the effective ConstitutionRepository.
Authenticated human identity accepts any non-empty binary as a valid credential and authenticated?/1 is a presence check on a self-asserted struct.
The AuditLog Merkle root has no located consumer anywhere in the repo, and degraded-mode reads (recent/chain_tip/merkle_root) fail soft while append fails closed.
The five-minute audit timeout requirement has no implementation and no owning subsystem; the only 5-minute timeout in governance code governs validation campaigns, not constitutional audits.
discrepancies.evidence: R0_SOURCE_PLAN.txt:1147; os/governance/validation/campaign_executor.ex:72; audit_log.ex:40 is a Merkle interval.
